item.title: Introduction to Third-Party Login and Single Sign-On
item.description: The session mechanism for login: HTTP is a stateless protocol, and every request a browser makes is independent of the others. But not every HTTP request is unrelated to state, so the browser and the server have to jointly maintain a state — this is the session mechanism. One approach: the first time the browser sends a request to the server, the server returns a sessionID to the browser, and every subsequent request from the browser carries that sessionID to verify the same user.
